subject: history_social
passage: In a number of psychology experiments, two groups of students were given the same science passage and the same total amount of study time. One group spent the whole time rereading the passage, while the other read it once and then spent the remaining time writing down everything they could recall without looking back. Immediately afterward, the students who had reread predicted that they would remember more of the passage a week later than the students in the recall group predicted for themselves. A week later, however, it was the recall group that remembered substantially more. If these results hold generally, they suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: students' own sense of which study method works better may be an unreliable guide.
choices.B: rereading a passage does not help students remember any of its content.
choices.C: the students in the recall group spent more time studying than the students who reread.
choices.D: the recall group remembered more because they found the passage more interesting.

explanation.why: Compare the predictions with the results. The rereading group expected to remember more, but the recall group actually did. Students' confidence pointed to the weaker method, so how well students feel they have learned may not tell them which method works best.
explanation.A: Correct. The rereaders felt more confident yet remembered less, so students' impressions of which method works may mislead them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The rereaders remembered less than the recall group, not nothing; the results do not show rereading is useless.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says both groups had the same total study time.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never mentions how interesting the students found the passage.
